sections.title: Positioning
sections.summary: Amazon's seller site sells access: reach, fulfillment and a large new-seller incentive package, framed around helping independent sellers grow.
keyPoints: Homepage: 'Sell more with Amazon', with an offer of 10% back on your first $50,000 in branded sales.
A top banner repeats the pitch: unlock $50K in new seller credits, bonuses and exclusive benefits.
Proof is scale: more than 75,000 independent sellers surpassed $1 million in sales in 2025.

sections.title: Products and offerings
sections.summary: A marketplace selling account with a menu of fulfillment, advertising, brand and B2B programs around it.

rows: The right to list and sell in the Amazon store
Brand Registry, enhanced product pages, a digital store and Brand Analytics
Selling to business customers in larger quantities
Learn-and-build guide for creating a store with Amazon
Selling Partner Appstore and Seller app
Third-party apps and a mobile app to create listings and manage orders

sections.title: Pricing
sections.summary: Two selling plans plus category-based referral fees. Many costs, including fulfillment and advertising, are optional and priced separately.
keyPoints: Individual is pay-per-sale; Professional is a monthly subscription with bulk listing, advertising, brand and API features.
Referral fees vary by product category and are on their own tab, next to a revenue calculator.
After registration a seller can switch or cancel a plan at any time.
New sellers can get over $50,000 in credits, bonuses and benefits, marked with an asterisk.

rows: List one product at a time, static prices, FBA or fulfill yourself
Bulk operations, Amazon Ads, brand-building tools, Automate Pricing, Amazon Business, Global Selling, apps and APIs

gaps: Referral fee rates by category, FBA fees and advertising costs were not read.

sections.title: Merchandising
sections.summary: The offer is merchandised with a two-plan ladder, a large incentive and a three-question quiz. For sellers, Amazon provides some of the deepest selling tools in the survey.
keyPoints: A 'Not sure where to begin?' quiz asks three questions, starting with where your business is based.
Incentives are the main hook: 10% back on the first $50,000 in branded sales and over $50,000 in credits and benefits for new sellers.
Plan choice is simple: pay per item or pay monthly for bulk tools and advertising.
For merchants: Brand Analytics on customer search and purchase data, enhanced product pages, a digital store, Automate Pricing, advertising and B2B selling.

sections.title: Technical platform
sections.summary: The seller site points to apps and APIs and a Selling Partner Appstore; the surveyed pages carry little API detail, but the blog mentions an MCP-based advertising tool.
keyPoints: The Professional plan lists 'Sell with apps and APIs'.
The Selling Partner Appstore lists Amazon-approved third-party apps that connect to a selling account.
The Selling Partner Blog announces a Selling Partner plugin and an Ads MCP for holiday preparation.
gaps: No API documentation, rate limits or developer pages were surveyed.

sections.title: Design
sections.summary: Bold and orange: a very large headline, a pill-shaped orange button, an illustrated seller dashboard and a green incentives bar. The sign-in page drops to Amazon's plain account style.
keyPoints: Marketing pages use an Ember Modern typeface with orange (#ff6200) and a near-black (#161d26) and pill buttons (31.986px corners).
The home hero pairs a large two-tone headline with an illustrated Seller Central dashboard.
The pricing page uses a headline, a photo and rounded tab pills for plans, referral fees and the revenue calculator.
The sign-in page is plain Arial with a yellow (#ffd814) button.
Pages are comparatively short: the home page is 3,920px and pricing is 4,619px.
gaps: Merchant design control beyond the store builder was not surveyed.

sections.title: Company presentation
sections.summary: A seller-success story with a specific scale number, footnoted, and a content hub rather than a company page.
keyPoints: Home: more than 75,000 independent sellers surpassed $1 million in sales in 2025, with a footnote.
The pricing page cites 'Amazon internal data, FY2023, US store' for an FBA claim.
A Selling Partner Blog carries announcements and tips; no About or leadership page appeared.
gaps: No About page or leadership information in the surveyed pages.

signupPath: The homepage 'Sign up*' and the incentives banner lead to sellercentral.amazon.com/ap/signin, headed 'Start selling with Amazon'. It says 'To register, sign in with your existing Amazon account', asks for a mobile number or email with a Continue button, and links 'Create your Amazon account' for new users, with a Conditions of Use and Privacy Notice line. It is a sign-in step, not a seller registration form. Nothing was entered.

jtbd_fit.evidence: Everything is about selling products in the Amazon store.

capability_visible.evidence: A dashboard illustration, an overview video for Brand Analytics, a revenue calculator and a seller app page.

pricing_transparency.evidence: Two plans and a referral-fee tab are published; category rates, FBA and ad costs are separate.

product_breadth.evidence: Fulfillment, ads, brand tools, B2B, global selling and an appstore are explained.

platform_depth.evidence: Appstore and 'apps and APIs' are mentioned and a blog covers an Ads MCP; no developer docs were surveyed.

time_to_value.evidence: Capture stops before the product; first-value time was not observed.

friction.evidence: Registration requires signing in with an existing Amazon account; a separate link creates one.

trust.evidence: A scale number for sellers and an Amazon brand; claims are footnoted.

mobile.evidence: Phone captures exist for home and pricing but were not assessed.

states.evidence: No error or empty states reached.

value_prop_clarity.evidence: 'Sell more with Amazon' and the incentive line are plain.

proof_quality.evidence: Claims carry footnotes, but sources are 'Amazon internal data'.

persuasion_integrity.evidence: Most calls to action carry an asterisk against incentive terms.

cta_logic.evidence: A single orange 'Sign up' or 'Start selling' action on every page.

company_narrative.evidence: The story is entirely about seller success; the company itself is not presented.

offer_packaging.evidence: Two plans with a feature list each; the fee structure beyond them is spread across tabs.

offer_architecture.evidence: Incentive credits, cash back on branded sales, a pay-per-item entry, a monthly plan and optional fulfillment and ads.

merchant_merch_tools.evidence: Brand analytics, enhanced pages, a digital store, price automation, ads and B2B.

visual_craft.evidence: Strong hierarchy and a clear single action; the green incentives bar and orange headline compete.

system_coherence.evidence: Marketing pages use Ember Modern and pill buttons; sign-in uses Arial with a rectangular yellow button.

merchant_design_control.evidence: Enhanced product pages, a digital store and an online store builder guide.

read.summary: A marketplace pitch led by incentives rather than features: 10% back and over $50,000 in credits, a simple two-plan ladder and a deep toolset behind it. Registration requires an existing Amazon account, and most calls to action carry asterisks.
pros: Two plans with clear prices and a plain 'switch or cancel any time' note.
A calculator, quiz and referral-fee tab help sellers estimate cost.
The incentive offer is specific and repeated.
A deep set of brand, ad and B2B tools.
cons: Sign-in is required to register; account creation is a separate link.
Referral fees vary by category and are on a different tab.
Little developer detail on the surveyed pages.
read.howItSells: Sells access and money: reach, fulfillment, cash back and credits, with a scale number and a promise that Amazon runs the heavy parts.
copy: Lead with a specific incentive and say what it is worth.
Offer a pay-per-item plan next to a monthly plan.
Add a short quiz for newcomers.
avoid: Asterisks on every call to action.
A different look at the sign-in page.

hypothesis.statement: Showing an estimated first-year net amount from the incentives beside the sign-up button will lift registration starts among new sellers.
hypothesis.guardrail: Registration completion and early listing rate
hypothesis.decisionRule: Ship if click-through rises by a pre-agreed margin and completion holds over four weeks.

merchandising.summary: Incentive-led and plan-simple, backed by powerful seller tools, but dependent on asterisked terms.
pros: A three-question quiz and a revenue calculator.
Two plans with a plain upgrade story.

design.summary: Confident and clear on the marketing pages, with a plain, different look at sign-in.
pros: Big two-tone headlines and a dashboard picture make the offer concrete.
A single orange action is easy to find.
cons: The sign-in page looks like a different brand.
Orange headline and green banner compete.
